title_en: Chinese Humor (9/20): The Trouble with Sharing a Name
note_en: This text is full of the 被 passive: 小李的工资有一次被多打给了另一个李明 "Xiao Li's pay was once sent to the other Li Ming by mistake." Unlike the English passive, 被 usually signals something unwelcome happening to the subject, and the doer can be left out entirely, as here: what matters is the mix-up, not who caused it. When the doer is named, it comes right after 被: 被老师批评 "criticized by the teacher."
